extracted.intended_audience: legal scholars, students, historians, and the general public interested in English constitutional law
extracted.subtask_description: The statutory text of the English Bill of Rights (1689), setting out legal declarations limiting royal power, establishing parliamentary privileges, succession rules, and civil liberties. The page is a primary legal document whose provisions function as binding standards for governance and rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illegality of suspending laws without Parliament
rubrics_metrics.description: That the pretended power of suspending the laws or the execution of laws by regal authority without consent of Parliament is illegal;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibits monarchs from unilaterally suspending statutes or their execution; a fundamental restriction on royal prerogative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illegality of dispensing with laws by regal authority
rubrics_metrics.description: That the pretended power of dispensing with laws or the execution of laws by regal authority, as it hath been assumed and exercised of late, is illegal;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bars the monarch from dispensing with statutory obligations or enforcement absent parliamentary authorization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illegality of certain commissions and ecclesiastical courts
rubrics_metrics.description: That the commission for erecting the late Court of Commissioners for Ecclesiastical Causes, and all other commissions and courts of like nature, are illegal and pernicious;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declares particular royal-created ecclesiastical tribunals (and similar commissions) void as contrary to law and dangerous in effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illegal levying of money for Crown without Parliament
rubrics_metrics.description: That levying money for or to the use of the Crown by pretence of prerogative, without grant of Parliament, for longer time, or in other manner than the same is or shall be granted, is illegal;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affirms parliamentary control over taxation and public revenue; the Crown may not raise funds by prerogative beyond or contrary to parliamentary grants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to petition the king
rubrics_metrics.description: That it is the right of the subjects to petition the king, and all commitments and prosecutions for such petitioning are illegal;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects petitioning as a lawful right and forbids penalizing subjects for exercising it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on standing army without Parliament
rubrics_metrics.description: That the raising or keeping a standing army within the kingdom in time of peace, unless it be with consent of Parliament, is against law;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires parliamentary consent for a peacetime standing army; implicates quartering and maintenance of troops.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right of Protestants to have arms for defence
rubrics_metrics.description: That the subjects which are Protestants may have arms for their defence suitable to their conditions and as allowed by law;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits Protestants to possess arms consistent with their status and subject to existing law (qualification limited by 'as allowed by law').

rubrics_metrics.name: Free elections to Parliament
rubrics_metrics.description: That election of members of Parliament ought to be free;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes free election as an essential feature of representative government; implicitly condemns interference with electoral processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parliamentary privilege of free speech and debates
rubrics_metrics.description: That the freedom of speech and debates or proceedings in Parliament ought not to be impeached or questioned in any court or place out of Parliament;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides immunity for parliamentary speech and proceedings from external legal challenge or prosecution (speech and debate privilege).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on excessive bail, fines, and cruel/unusual punishment
rubrics_metrics.description: That excessive bail ought not to be required, nor excessive fines imposed, nor cruel and unusual punishments inflicted;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets proportionality and humanity standards in criminal procedure and sentencing; forbids punitive measures beyond reasonable bounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper impaneling and qualifications of jurors
rubrics_metrics.description: That jurors ought to be duly impanelled and returned, and jurors which pass upon men in trials for high treason ought to be freeholders;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires lawful selection and return of jurors; for high treason trials, jurors must be freeholders (a property qualification).

rubrics_metrics.name: Invalidity of grants/promises of fines or forfeitures before conviction
rubrics_metrics.description: That all grants and promises of fines and forfeitures of particular persons before conviction are illegal and void;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevents pre-judgment grants or assignments of fines/forfeitures targeted at specific persons prior to conviction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frequent Parliaments for redress and law maintenance
rubrics_metrics.description: And that for redress of all grievances, and for the amending, strengthening and preserving of the laws, Parliaments ought to be held frequently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affirms regular parliamentary sessions as necessary for governance, grievance redress, and legislative maintenance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition of dispensing with statutes by non obstante (Section II)
rubrics_metrics.description: That from and after this present session of Parliament no dispensation by non obstante of or to any statute or any part thereof shall be allowed, but that the same shall be held void and of no effect, except a dispensation be allowed of in such statute, and except in such cases as shall be specially provided for by one or more bill or bills to be passed during this present session of Parliament.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forbids use of 'non obstante' (royal dispensation) to override statutes; only Parliament can create exceptions by statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation of prior charters/grants/pardons (Section III)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provided that no charter or grant or pardon granted before the three and twentieth day of October in the year of our Lord one thousand six hundred eighty-nine shall be any ways impeached or invalidated by this Act, but that the same shall be and remain of the same force and effect in law and no other than as if this Act had never been made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects the legal force of pre-existing charters, grants, and pardons from being invalidated by this Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condemnation of quartering soldiers contrary to law and illegal disarming
rubrics_metrics.description: By raising and keeping a standing army within this kingdom in time of peace without consent of Parliament, and quartering soldiers contrary to law; By causing several good subjects being Protestants to be disarmed at the same time when papists were both armed and employed contrary to law;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Denounces illegal quartering of troops and discriminatory disarmament; these practices are listed among abuses contrary to the laws and liberties of the realm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition of prosecutions of matters cognizable only in Parliament
rubrics_metrics.description: By prosecutions in the Court of King's Bench for matters and causes cognizable only in Parliament, and by divers other arbitrary and illegal courses;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Asserts that certain matters fall exclusively to Parliament's cognizance and should not be prosecuted in ordinary courts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excessive bail and fines used to elude legal liberties
rubrics_metrics.description: And excessive bail hath been required of persons committed in criminal cases to elude the benefit of the laws made for the liberty of the subjects; And excessive fines have been imposed;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies the use of excessive bail/fines as tools to deny legal protections; condemns these practices as contrary to liberty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement of declarations and oaths renouncing papal deposition doctrine
rubrics_metrics.description: "I, A.B., do swear that I do from my heart abhor, detest and abjure as impious and heretical this damnable doctrine and position, that princes excommunicated or deprived by the Pope or any authority of the see of Rome may be deposed or murdered by their subjects or any other whatsoever..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates a formal declaration renouncing the doctrine that papal actions can justify deposition or murder of princes, and denies papal jurisdiction within the realm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Succession and limitation excluding papists from the crown
rubrics_metrics.description: That all and every person and persons that is, are or shall be reconciled to or shall hold communion with the see or Church of Rome, or shall profess the popish religion, or shall marry a papist, shall be excluded and be for ever incapable to inherit, possess or enjoy the crown and government of this realm and Ireland and the dominions thereunto belonging...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legally excludes Catholics and those who marry Catholics from succession and from exercising regal authority; declares the people absolved of allegiance in such cases and provides that the crown shall descend to qualified Protestant heirs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for new monarchs to make prescribed declarations
rubrics_metrics.description: That every king and queen of this realm who at any time hereafter shall come to and succeed in the imperial crown of this kingdom shall on the first day of the meeting of the first Parliament next after his or her coming to the crown... make, subscribe and audibly repeat the declaration mentioned in the statute made in the thirtieth year of the reign of King Charles the Second...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imposes procedural obligations on incoming monarchs to publicly make and subscribe to specified declarations (religious/political) at Parliament or coronation, with age exceptions.
